title: CS aggregation & scope primer for enterprise feature asks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Sales and CS receive many enterprise non-bug feature requests that repeat, conflict, or lack scoping detail. That creates churn for PM and Eng and slows prioritization for Dedicated/Private customers. Goal: deliver a lightweight, repeatable aggregation + initial scoping primer that Sales/CS can run in 30–60 minutes and hand to PMs as a bounded, prioritized intake artifact.

Scope: playbook covers (1) a 3-tier aggregation rubric, (2) a one-page scoping template, (3) account-aware prioritization signals, (4) an automated CSV export format for the intake queue, and (5) a short training slide deck + a one-hour pilot workshop with two AE teams. Not in scope: full PRD or engineering implementation work (those are downstream).

Unique approach: instead of a long PRD-first flow, this primer uses a decision-tree that maps ask -> minimum viable scope (MVS) + risk buckets (compliance/infra/data residency) and provides a rough cost multiplier (latency/capacity estimate) so PMs can estimate impact quickly. The rubric intends to reduce back-and-forth and give Sales/CS a clear "what we need to triage" checklist.
